title: Bollywood Stars, Faith Groups Rally Behind India's Gen Z Protest
excerpt: From Diljit Dosanjh to Shabana Azmi, celebrities, Sikh community groups, and diaspora supporters join the Cockroach Janta Party's growing movement after a police crackdown at Delhi's Jantar Mantar.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Bollywood stars like Diljit Dosanjh and Shabana Azmi support the CJP protest after police violence.
  • Sikh community groups provide food and medical aid to sustain the protest at Jantar Mantar.
  • The Modi government is engaging with protesters, promising reforms and accountability.
  • Youth unemployment is at 9.9%, fueling the most significant challenge to Modi's government.
Bollywood's Solidarity
›Over a dozen celebrities joined the protest.
›Shabana Azmi and Prakash Raj participated physically.
›Diljit Dosanjh condemned police actions on social media.
›Hrithik Roshan shared a video supporting hunger-striking activist.

India's youth-led Cockroach Janta Party protest, initially dismissed as social media satire, has drawn an expanding coalition of support from Bollywood celebrities, religious communities, and overseas Indians — transforming a student grievance into the most serious public challenge to Prime Minister Narendra Modi's third-term government.

https://x.com/ShekharGupta/status/2080261629917417710

Bollywood Breaks Its Silence

The police crackdown on July 20, when officers used tear gas and lathi-charges against tens of thousands of protesters marching on parliament, triggered a wave of condemnation from India's entertainment industry.

Veteran actress Shabana Azmi and actor Prakash Raj physically joined the demonstration at Jantar Mantar, with Azmi reportedly falling ill from the heat. Actor-singer Diljit Dosanjh posted on Instagram that the treatment of students was "very wrong" and said he expected to be labeled "anti-national" for speaking up — a reference to backlash he faced after supporting the 2020-21 farmers' protest.

"Our students need embracing hands, not lathis."

— Sonu Sood, actor

Hrithik Roshan reshared a video of hunger-striking activist Sonam Wangchuk, writing: "This sounds true. I learnt about the trauma students go through when I played a teacher in one of my movies." Filmmaker Anurag Kashyap, actors Huma Qureshi, Sonakshi Sinha, Bhumi Pednekar, and musician Vishal Dadlani all condemned the police action. Riteish and Genelia Deshmukh issued a joint statement: "Their voices deserve to be heard — loud, clear, and without fear."

Community Networks Sustain the Sit-In

Beyond celebrity endorsements, an organic support infrastructure has kept the protest running around the clock. A steady stream of food delivery riders ferries meals and water from supporters across India and as far as the United States, according to Reuters.

"From Kerala to the USA, orders are coming from everywhere."

— Suraj Kumar, 25, food delivery rider at Jantar Mantar

Sikh community groups have been part of the support base, according to Bloomberg, with gurdwaras extending their tradition of langar — free communal meals — to sustain protesters. The CJP held an early rally in Amritsar, the Sikh holy city, and video footage shows Sikh volunteers at the Delhi site. A medical stall staffed by volunteer doctors and students has operated at Jantar Mantar for about a month.

So much food poured in that organizers asked people to stop sending further contributions, according to The Times. "This protest is running purely because of people's kindness, and the fact that we are all united," Delhi University student Rina Rawat, 20, told Reuters. She returned to volunteer the day after being struck by police batons.

Government Shows Signs of Engagement

The movement centers on the NEET-UG medical entrance exam paper leak in May, which forced two million students to resit the test. A dozen students reportedly took their own lives. The CJP demands Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation, compensation for bereaved families, and that Wangchuk — forcibly moved to hospital on July 19 after losing nine kilograms during his hunger strike — be allowed to address supporters.

Community Support Fuels Protest
›Sikh groups provide langar meals to protesters.
›Food deliveries come from across India and the USA.
›Medical aid is provided by volunteer doctors.
›Protesters received so much food that contributions were halted.

After initially refusing to engage, the government shifted. Health Minister JP Nadda met CJP spokesperson Saurav Das, and Pradhan promised "answers, reforms and accountability." Opposition leader Rahul Gandhi was detained during a protest outside the prime minister's residence.

"This level of anger suggests a wider dissatisfaction with Modi and how the government functions," political commentator Parsa Venkateshwar Rao Jr told The Times. "What we're seeing now is something above and beyond a protest about a paper leak."

What's Next

On Wednesday, around 5,000 protesters remained at Jantar Mantar despite monsoon rains. From hospital, Wangchuk set conditions for ending his fast, including lawmakers assuring him they would address the education system's failures in parliament's current session.

The CJP, which has amassed 22 million Instagram followers, faces the challenge of converting online energy into lasting political pressure. Youth unemployment stands at 9.9% among Indians aged 15 to 29, rising to 13.6% in urban areas — in a country where more than half the 1.42 billion population is under 30.

Government's Response to Protests
›Health Minister JP Nadda met with CJP representatives.
›Education Minister Pradhan promised reforms.
›CJP demands accountability for the NEET-UG exam crisis.
›Opposition leader Rahul Gandhi was detained during protests.

"It feels like the beginning of something," political researcher Asim Ali told The Times. "Once you lose the trust of young people, whether it's over unemployment or corruption, anything can happen, as we have seen in Bangladesh and Nepal."

nri_angle: Overseas Indians are supporting the protest by ordering food deliveries to the Jantar Mantar site from the United States and other countries, while the movement's focus on education reform resonates with diaspora families navigating competitive pressures in both India and abroad.
author: Diaspora Desk
